subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should plain provider `api_error: Internal server error` be classified for cron/fallback behavior: `server_error`, `overloaded`, `timeout`, or a cron-local transient that avoids shared auth-profile cooldown?
rationale: Each classification changes retry matching, fallback escalation, and whether shared auth-profile cooldown state is affected, so a narrow regex patch would encode product policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use cron-local outage classification
options.body: Treat the plain provider 500 as retryable for cron/fallback without marking shared auth profiles unhealthy unless maintainers explicitly opt in.

options.title: Map it to `server_error`
options.body: Reuse the structured server-error path so cron state and retry policy report provider 500s consistently while avoiding overload cooldown semantics.

options.title: Map it to `overloaded`
options.body: Skip same-provider profiles sooner through existing overload cooldown behavior, accepting profile-health side effects during broad HTTP 500 outages.

recommendation.title: Use cron-local outage classification
recommendation.body: Treat the plain provider 500 as retryable for cron/fallback without marking shared auth profiles unhealthy unless maintainers explicitly opt in.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the closest merged structured server-error retry/classification follow-up and the overloaded failover behavior this decision would affect.
